nodes.label: MapAnything (facebook/map-anything-apache)
nodes.rationale: Purpose-built for metric scale and matches VGGT end-to-end once its threshold is calibrated; runs in an isolated spatialdiff-ma env because its dependency pins conflict with the main env; the Apache-2.0 checkpoint keeps the stack commercially usable.

nodes.label: VGGT (facebook/VGGT-1B)
nodes.rationale: Feed-forward reconstruction of multiple frames into one shared coordinate frame - exactly what 'reconstruct both videos together' needs; CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial).

nodes.label: Backend comparison: VGGT vs MapAnything vs DA3
nodes.norm_label: backend comparison: vggt vs mapanything vs da3

nodes.label: Backend-agnostic artifact contract
nodes.rationale: VGGT and MapAnything write the same cache artifact contract ({cameras,dense,colors}.npz + meta.json), so every downstream stage is backend-agnostic; MapAnything can therefore run in an isolated conda env as a subprocess.

nodes.label: Depth Anything 3 integration chain (five fixes)
nodes.rationale: MapAnything's hydra configs must shadow the pip package before the first import, external wrappers use forward() and need views on device, the raw unified output needs MapAnything's postprocess, and dtype names need mapping; the Apache-2.0 DA3-LARGE-1.1 checkpoint was selected over the default CC-BY-NC GIANT.

nodes.label: Thin-object finding (comb/pen below VGGT patch scale)
nodes.norm_label: thin-object finding (comb/pen below vggt patch scale)
nodes.rationale: The 1 cm-thick comb and pen are below VGGT's ~1.4 cm patch scale and are absent from the depth maps (their z equals the table's); any threshold that would see them is below the reconstruction noise. This forced the photometric tabletop diff.

nodes.label: Timing audit (wrong numbers corrected)
nodes.rationale: A user-visible mismatch triggered a full audit of PBS records and job logs; unverifiable timing claims were corrected and the README now carries measured runtime tables with conditions instead of single numbers.

nodes.label: VLM verification over-confirmation fixes
nodes.rationale: Tighter verification crops, pose-matched other-view frames, a self-consistency override, mutual cancellation, a score floor, a replaced pixel gate and fragment merging were added because the VLM confirmed the untouched timer, the highlighter and tiny fragments.

nodes.label: Nothing is ever silently dropped
nodes.rationale: Every rejection is written to cache/semantics/rejected.json with a human-readable reason and survivors to confirmed.json, so the 26-to-3 candidate reduction is fully auditable.

nodes.label: Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct
nodes.rationale: Best open VLM available here for short object labels and fluent descriptions; ~64 GB in bf16 needs 2 A100s (device_map=auto); the 8B variant is the fast fallback.

nodes.label: Results across all scenes (9/9 development changes)
nodes.norm_label: results across all scenes (9/9 development changes)

nodes.label: Cache invalidation rules
nodes.rationale: --force re-runs a stage and overwrites its outputs; describe always reuses cached Qwen3-VL answers keyed by model (delete cache/semantics to force fresh calls); changing tabletop thresholds only needs diff --force; changing frames.* invalidates everything downstream.

nodes.label: Automatic diff-mode choice
nodes.rationale: detect.py measures the dominant plane coverage of confident points (+/-2 cm); >=50% coverage selects tabletop, otherwise geometric; the choice and measured coverage are printed and --method overrides it.

nodes.label: Geometric diff mode
nodes.rationale: Voxel-downsample both clouds, bidirectional nearest-neighbour distance, outlier removal, DBSCAN clustering, then a visibility check using cached poses+depth; good for objects at least 2-3 cm thick.

nodes.label: Natural-language summary stage
nodes.rationale: Reads report.json only; one Qwen3-VL phrasing call whose sentences are validated against the label, the type's action vocabulary and a non-object word list, with a deterministic template fallback; low-confidence entries get 'Possibly ...'.

nodes.label: Tabletop photometric diff mode
nodes.rationale: Appearance comparison over the fitted dominant plane: needed because objects thinner than VGGT's patch scale (the 1 cm comb and pen) are absent from the depth maps; outputs the same cluster format as the geometric mode.

nodes.label: Held-out protocol
nodes.rationale: Freeze the detection files (sha256) per held-out scene, run it exactly once cold with defaults and no overrides, commit the outputs as produced; any later change is post-hoc, labelled and reported separately.

nodes.label: Pre-registered scoring rule
nodes.rationale: A ground-truth change counts as FOUND only if the type matches, the evidence overlay shows the right object, and the label names it correctly; label correctness, extras and unverified candidates are counted separately. Written before the run.

nodes.label: Held-out scenes and post-hoc changes rule
nodes.norm_label: held-out scenes and post-hoc changes rule
nodes.rationale: A held-out scene is run exactly once cold with frozen detection code and default settings; no fix may touch the frozen files for that scene's result; later changes are labelled post-hoc and reported separately.

nodes.label: Gotcha 1: PBS hides GPUs via empty CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
nodes.norm_label: gotcha 1: pbs hides gpus via empty cuda_visible_devices

nodes.label: Git LFS for large binaries
nodes.rationale: Videos, point clouds and model weights go through Git LFS; reproducible artifacts (cache/, outputs/*, models/) are gitignored and not committed at all.

nodes.label: Critical rules (read first)
nodes.rationale: Use GPU nodes for all large-model work; cache every expensive result so later stages re-run without a GPU; one working stage at a time; keep every model name, path and threshold in configs/default.yaml; never fabricate results; ship a public GitHub repository.

nodes.label: Config as single source of tunables
nodes.norm_label: config as single source of tunables
nodes.rationale: Every model name, path and threshold lives in configs/default.yaml; scripts must not hard-code values, so a scene can be re-tuned without code changes.

nodes.label: Non-negotiables
nodes.rationale: No fabricated numbers (every number comes from a real run), all thresholds in configs/default.yaml, follow the held-out protocol, devlog everything including failures, GPU policy (use idle GPUs, never wait on a busy one, stop/restart the gpu-session), and tag from main as v<major>.<minor>.<bugs>.

nodes.label: Honesty rule (no invented results)
nodes.rationale: No document may contain results, metrics or screenshots that did not come from a real run; until a run happens, sections say so explicitly.

nodes.label: Checkpoint discipline
nodes.rationale: A checkpoint is only done when it passes on real data; code that exists but has not been validated end-to-end is marked partial.

nodes.label: DINOv2 (facebook/dinov2-large)
nodes.rationale: Robust self-supervised crop embeddings for deciding that two detections are the same object moved, not two different changes.

nodes.label: DINOv2 move matching
nodes.rationale: A removed cluster and an added cluster with high crop-embedding similarity but different 3D positions become one moved object instead of two separate changes.

nodes.label: Joint reconstruction design decision
nodes.rationale: Both videos are reconstructed together in a single VGGT run so every frame lands in one coordinate frame, avoiding fragile cross-run registration.

nodes.label: Occlusion-aware visibility check
nodes.rationale: A cluster counts as removed only if the other video actually observed that space and saw it empty (cached poses + depth); merely occluded or unseen clusters are discarded to suppress false positives.

nodes.label: Move/arrival/composite semantics (v0.10.0)
nodes.rationale: Move matching now runs right after VLM confirmation, arrivals at a move's origin are reported as added, replaced claims whose two sides are independently confirmed changes are dropped as composites, and the match threshold is 0.65 with the VLM move question as arbiter.

nodes.label: Gotcha 3: FIFO cannot bridge login and GPU nodes

nodes.label: Clone on the shared home filesystem
nodes.norm_label: clone on the shared home filesystem
nodes.rationale: A clone under /tmp is node-local: detect.py on the login node would submit a PBS job that runs on another machine and cannot see the files; git-lfs is installed on the login node only.

nodes.label: CUDA 12.6 (cu126) PyTorch requirement
nodes.rationale: The 525.147.05 driver supports max CUDA 12.3, so CUDA-13 torch builds fail; cu126 wheels work via minor-version compatibility and keep recent torch versions that newer models need.

nodes.label: Install torch from the cu126 index first
nodes.norm_label: install torch from the cu126 index first
nodes.rationale: Torch must be installed first from the cu126 index because CUDA-13 builds fail on the 525 driver; requirements.txt then pins the rest of the pipeline (numpy<2 for VGGT).

nodes.label: HPC resource-use rules
nodes.rationale: GPUs are shared: check nvidia-smi and pick an idle GPU, never wait on a busy one, report an estimated remaining time for every GPU job, respect PBS limits, and remember the per-user 16-CPU quota is the real bottleneck.

nodes.label: Synthetic smoke-test fixtures
nodes.rationale: Development fixtures let the CPU stages be smoke-tested before real recordings exist; nothing produced from them counts as a project result.
